title: AB Matrix Orchestrator: Console sketches for interleaved experiment lanes and graceful unwind
creator: Sienna Cho
description: Problem: product and infra teams need a compact console surface to compose multi-variant A/B experiments that can run interleaved (time-boxed windows), support staged traffic splits across cohorts, and provide a fast, human-in-the-loop unwind (rollback) that preserves downstream analytics. Current visualizations in the Console are focused on single-variant canaries or linear splits; this flow shows a matrix-first authoring surface that treats experiments as a lattice of lanes and windows. Goals: 1) let engineers/PMs define multiple variants and cohorts, schedule overlapping windows, and preview expected distribution over time; 2) make rollback a first-class, low-friction operation that can target specific cells (variant X cohort Y window) without tearing down unrelated traffic; 3) surface cost and latency impact per variant so teams can balance quality vs. unit economics; 4) keep UI compact for common tasks and expandable for power users (details-on-demand). Constraints: must work with existing rollout APIs (traffic-slice, canary-window, variant-fallback), require minimal backend schema changes—prefer composition via existing routing rules and an authoring layer; must support RBAC and audit logs for enterprise customers. User story: As an SRE or PM I want to create an experiment with three variants and two cohorts, schedule two overlapping windows, and be able to pause only the cohort experiencing errors and shift traffic to a safe fallback while preserving metrics continuity. Prototype summary: - Canvas: grid with vertical lanes = cohorts, horizontal timeline = windows; cells represent variant allocations. - Composer: drag-to-expand windows, numeric traffic inputs per cell, quick presets (equal / cost-aware / latency-priority). - Inspector overlay: quick metrics for selected cell (p50 latency, error rate, token cost delta, active requests) plus an action bar (pause, scale-down, divert to fallback, snapshot). - Safe-unwind modal: shows deterministic effects of unwind (which cohorts get reverted, expected traffic ripples) and highlights downstream analytics continuity risks. - Audit & rollback trace: generate a reversible operation id with links to traces and dashboard slices. Edge cases: overlapping scheduled windows must show precedence rules; default is latest-scheduled wins unless explicit priority set. Accessibility: keyboard-first composer mode and high-contrast variants on timeline. Metrics: decrease mean time to rollback (MTTR) for experiments by 30% (goal), reduce accidental full-release rollbacks by surfacing targeted rollback options.
decisions: Authoring will be implemented client-side as composition of existing routing rules; no new API required for MVP
Pause action will create a reversible operation id that maps to a sequence of existing API calls (traffic-slice updates + snapshot)
Default cell precedence rule: last-modified wins; explicit priority can be set per window (UI exposes priority toggle)
Cost telemetry shown per-cell will use sampled cost estimates from runtime telemetry and not live billing data in MVP
risks: Backend: complex overlapping-window conflict resolution may need server-side validation in later iterations
Product: exposing too many knobs increases cognitive load for non-expert teams
Security: reversible operation ids require strict audit trail; must be added to enterprise audit logging scope
